InFigure3.18,the gas turbine load factor, marked y, and the ambient temperature TSet are the two inputs that govern the variations in the efficiency of electric power generation and fuel mass flow rate, aswellastheflowandtemperatureoftheexhaustgas. Specifically,eachoutputisdeterminedbymultiplyingthenominalvaluebyitscorresponding part load correction factor, where the correction factor is obtained from the look-up tables. For example, the nominal value for the exhaust temperature is 522°C (at full load with an ambient temperature of 15°C); with a correction factor of 1.068, a load factor of 0.6 and an ambient temperature of 18°C, the resulting exhaust temperature TExh is approximately 558°C. Similarly, mExh can be determined using the same approach. The power output of the gas turbine PEle is obtained by multiplying the gas turbine load factor by the nominal value of the generation of electric power.
